summary: Structured output: schema mismatch error after copying older docs snippet (JSON schema versioning/shape drift)
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports a schema mismatch error when using Structured Output after copy/pasting an older docs snippet. The error appears immediately on request validation.

Impact
- Blocks customer from adopting Structured Output.
- Confusing because customer believes request matches docs; turns out snippet was from an older page / cached blog post referencing a deprecated request shape.

Customer report (verbatim-ish)
“We’re sending JSON schema to `response_format` like the docs example, but the API returns a schema mismatch error. Same code works in a coworker’s environment with a different snippet.”

Environment
- Hosted API: prod, us-east
- Client: Python (requests), not using official SDK
- Network: standard internet egress (no proxy noted)

What the customer tried
Customer copied an example that used an older structured output format (legacy fields and older naming). In their payload they were sending a schema object that the gateway now rejects due to shape/version mismatch.

Observed error
- HTTP status: 400 (customer reported) / 422 (support reproduced depending on payload)
- Error message: "structured_output schema mismatch" / "response_format.json_schema invalid"
- Gateway rejection happens before model execution.

Steps to reproduce (Support reproduction)
1) Use older snippet (customer provided) that sets structured output fields using legacy naming.
2) Send a request to the Chat/Responses endpoint with that payload.
3) Observe validation error from gateway mentioning schema mismatch/invalid schema.

Initial triage notes
Likely docs drift: older snippet references a schema shape that no longer matches the current gateway validator. Customer may be mixing:
- old docs snippet (legacy JSON schema wrapper)
- newer API behavior requiring explicit schema versioning/name fields (or stricter JSON schema subset)

Requested from customer
- Full request payload with secrets removed
- Request ID(s) from response headers
- Confirmation of the docs link/source where snippet was copied

Resolution approach
1) Provide corrected canonical example link (redwood-examples + updated docs page).
2) Explain schema versioning strategy: keep a `schema_id`/`schema_version` in customer code, bump version when schema changes, and pin it in app releases.
3) Clarify strict validation behavior and recommend a validation + retry strategy if they are parsing model output into structured data.

Support outcome
Customer confirmed the issue was caused by a cached/older docs snippet. After switching to the canonical example and updating their payload, requests succeeded.

Follow-ups
- Ensure the updated docs page includes an explicit note: “Older snippets used legacy request shapes; use the `json_schema` structured output mode shown below. If you are referencing saved snippets, re-check against this page.”
- Add a short FAQ entry on schema mismatch errors and how to version schemas (tracked in docs refresh workstream).
comments: 2026-01-20 (Dev Patel, Support): Ticket created from inbound email. Customer reports "schema mismatch" when enabling structured output. Asked for request payload + source link for snippet and any request IDs.
2026-01-20 (Customer, Alpine Metrics): Shared sanitized payload + screenshot of error. Snippet source: internal wiki page that copied Redwood docs ~3 months ago (no longer matches current docs).

2026-01-21 (Wei Chen, Docs/Support): Confirmed payload matches older docs shape. Pointed customer to canonical structured output example and updated docs page. Shared Confluence guidelines on JSON schema subset/constraints and advised adding `schema_version` to their own schema definitions.

2026-01-21 (Wei Chen): Reproduced locally: legacy snippet fails at gateway validation; canonical snippet succeeds. Noted error copy could be clearer; linked to ongoing example refresh and OpenAPI shape clarification.

2026-01-22 (Henry Cho, Product): Confirmed user-facing terminology: “Structured Output” (not “JSON mode”) and we should explicitly call out that request validation is strict and will reject incompatible schema wrappers. OK to add brief note about schema versioning in docs.

2026-01-23 (Dev Patel, Support): Customer confirmed fix: using the new canonical snippet resolved error. They asked how to prevent this recurring. Advised pinning schema versions in code and avoiding copy/paste from cached pages; use docs canonical URLs.
2026-01-28 (Wei Chen): Marking closed. Docs updates tracked in ENG-2846; canonical example references included in redwood-docs PR_903 and redwood-examples refresh.
resolution: Root cause: customer used an older/cached docs snippet with a legacy structured output schema wrapper that no longer matches gateway validation. Resolution: directed customer to updated canonical structured output examples and clarified schema versioning/pinning guidance; customer updated payload and confirmed success.
